headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network access make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; compliance risk is lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, while marketingskills references shared context and files. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed, so I choose medium over low due to default file-based coupling.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or shared skill files, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF agent_b consumes agent_a-written markdown or context as authoritative guidance, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable shared skill/context directories.
Require provenance tags on inter-agent file handoffs.
Review any file content before copying between agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code, open editor buffers, and workspace files with broad network egress; marketingskills reads and writes skill files and calls external sites. If they share a filesystem, sensitive code or buffers can flow into marketing artifacts or outbound requests. This is a default-pathway inference from documented file and egress surfaces, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace, files touched by agent_a can be read by agent_b.
IF agent_b uploads or republishes shared files to allowlisted external services, source code or editor-buffer content can leak outward.
mitigations: Use separate repositories or folders.
Exclude secrets and source trees from agent_b inputs.
Turn off outbound calls for agent_b during shared-workspace tasks.
Audit file diffs before any publish step.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and spawn subprocesses, and Continue explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances. That means concurrent edits to the same directory can race, overwrite, or corrupt artifacts without locking. Because the overlap is in default documented capabilities and can affect shared mutable state, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF either agent edits shared skill or workspace files without locking, state corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize write access with a simple manual lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo.
Check git or file diffs after each agent finishes.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code or workspace edits, and marketingskills is designed to build on shared context and reference each other. That makes it plausible for one agent’s output to become the other’s input without verification, causing errors to propagate across work products. The pathway exists in documented behavior, but downstream harm is not inherently irreversible, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative context, mistakes can cascade into later outputs.
IF agent_a writes files that agent_b later reuses without review, errors can be amplified across tasks.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require explicit verification of facts before reuse.
Keep agent outputs in separate staging files.
Limit agent_b to drafting, not final publication.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between stages.

E_compliance.rationale: Continue is an IDE assistant handling source code and editor buffers, while marketingskills handles marketing content and product marketing context. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance risk is visible from the profiles. I do not cite both agents beyond their data classes because this is a single-pipeline compliance check, not a direct interaction claim.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace, compliance obligations may change.
IF either agent logs or retains shared content longer than the operator expects, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review retention settings before use.
Use separate storage for sensitive and marketing materials.
Document which data classes each agent may touch.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both tools.
